notes: SEED, labeled from chunk snippets not probable causes, so verify. Excluded WPR19LA204 (bounced landing, no bird) and the deer-strike report (wildlife, not bird).

query: plane crashed because pilot got disoriented in clouds
notes: SEED, labeled from chunk snippets, verify. Spatial disorientation / loss of control in IMC. Excluded the water-rescue and hard-landing false positives.

Rule: turbulence must be a named factor AND loss/lack of control. Counted wake turbulence and jet wash as turbulence. Excluded spatial-disorientation-in-IMC cases that did NOT name turbulence, and runway directional-control events.

query: ran out of fuel and the engine quit
notes: Rule: fuel exhaustion OR fuel starvation only. Excluded fuel contamination (fuel present but dirty), mechanical causes, mixture-leaning, and undetermined power loss.

query: hard landing that damaged the airplane
notes: SATURATED query: 21 of 23 candidates are hard landings, so Recall@5 is structurally low here (denominator 21); read Hit@5 and MRR instead. Excluded a ground loop and a fatigue-crack gear failure.

query: lost control maneuvering at low altitude
notes: Rule: loss of control or stall WHILE maneuvering low. Excluded controlled-flight-into-terrain and wire/powerline collisions where the cause was failure to maintain clearance rather than loss of control.
SATURATED query: 22 of 23 are carb icing. Read Hit@5 and MRR, not Recall@5. Excluded one undetermined power-loss case.
Rule: contamination of fuel (water, debris, DEF, etc) causing power loss. Excluded a fuel-nozzle maintenance case that caused starvation rather than contamination.
Rule: high density altitude named as cause or contributing factor. Excluded pure weight-and-balance and undetermined-loss-of-control cases that did not name density altitude.
Rule: WAKE turbulence / wake vortex specifically. Deliberately excluded clear-air and convective turbulence, which are a different phenomenon, even though the word 'turbulence' matches.

KEY DISTINCTION: tail rotor FAILURE (mechanical: driveshaft, blade, components, bearings) is relevant. Loss of tail rotor EFFECTIVENESS (LTE) is an aerodynamic/pilot condition, NOT a failure, so all LTE cases were excluded even though they match on words.
Rule: power loss due to magneto fault/failure. Excluded undetermined power loss. Trap excluded: ERA17LA163 is a tachometer MAGNET assembly, not a magneto.

Strict rule: actual in-flight fire AND after takeoff. Excluded power-loss-without-fire (the majority), a brake fire, an engine-START fire, and a pre-takeoff fire. Note: the probable-cause sheet corrected a chunk-snippet error, CEN19MA190 looked like an explosion in the chunk but its cause is a thrust reduction with no fire.
SATURATED query: 22 of 23 are gear collapses. Read Hit@5 and MRR, not Recall@5. Excluded one pure hard-landing case with no gear collapse.
Rule: in-flight collision between two aircraft. Counted air-race and formation-flight collisions. Excluded in-flight breakups, stalls, and CFIT with no second aircraft.

query: stall spin during base to final turn
notes: Rule: stall/spin while maneuvering in the pattern or turning to land. Excluded intentional stall demonstrations, training maneuvers, and low-altitude aerobatic stalls not tied to the landing pattern. Judgment-heavy query.
KEY DISTINCTION: CFIT means the aircraft was under control when it hit terrain/water/wires. Excluded CEN18FA003 because its cause is LOSS of control, which by definition is not 'controlled' flight.
